record.original_question: For a br-graph H, let S_H be its switching graph. A k-ary weak near unanimity polymorphism is an idempotent polymorphism phi, for k >= 3, such that phi(x, x, ..., x, y) = phi(x, x, ..., y, x) = ... = phi(y, x, ..., x, x), and it is conservative when phi(v_1, ..., v_k) is always one of the inputs. Calling a polymorphism of S_H semi-conservative when it preserves symmetric lists, is it true that S_H has a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if S_H has a conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism?

evidence.quote: Let H be a br-graph, and S be the set {0, 1}. The switching graph SH of H is the br-graph on the set V(H) x S.

An idempotent polymorphism phi : H^k -> H, for k >= 3 is weak near unanimity or WNU if for every choice of x, y in V(H) we have phi(x, x, . . . , x, y) = phi(x, x, . . . , y, x) = . . . phi(y, x, . . . , x, x).
It is conservative if phi(v1, . . . , vk) in {v1, . . . , vk}.
Calling a polymorphism of SH semi-conservative if it conserves symmetric lists.
Question 6.1. Is it true for a br-graph H that (ii) SH has a semi-conservative WNU-polymorphism if and only if it has a conservative WNU-polymorphism?
We now have countless counterexamples giving negative answers to these last two questions.
Proposition 6.2. Where T is the br-graph on the left of Figure 3, PT has a semi-conservative WNU-polymorphism but no conservative WNU-polymorphism or semi-conservative 3-NU-polymorphism.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. A br-graph is a graph in which each vertex is labeled either black or red (so V(H) is partitioned into B(H) ∪ R(H)). A homomorphism between br-graphs preserves both edges and vertex colors. For a br-graph H, define its switching graph S_H as the br-graph with vertex set V(H) × {0,1}, where the edges and color labels are determined by H according to the standard switching construction (so that homomorphisms G → S_H correspond to "switchings" of homomorphisms into H).

Polymorphisms. For k ≥ 1, a k-ary polymorphism of a br-graph G is a homomorphism φ : G^k → G (where G^k is the categorical product in the category of br-graphs). It is idempotent if φ(x, x, …, x) = x for every x ∈ V(G). For k ≥ 3, an idempotent polymorphism φ is a weak near unanimity (WNU) polymorphism if, for all x, y ∈ V(G),
   φ(y, x, x, …, x) = φ(x, y, x, …, x) = ⋯ = φ(x, x, …, x, y).
A polymorphism φ is conservative if φ(v_1, …, v_k) ∈ {v_1, …, v_k} for all choices of v_i.

For the switching graph S_H, a list on S_H is a subset L ⊆ V(S_H) = V(H) × {0,1}. Such a list L is called symmetric if (v, 0) ∈ L ⇔ (v, 1) ∈ L for every v ∈ V(H). A polymorphism φ of S_H is semi-conservative if for every symmetric list L and every (v_1, …, v_k) ∈ L^k one has φ(v_1, …, v_k) ∈ L (equivalently, φ preserves all symmetric lists).

Question. Is it true that, for every br-graph H, the switching graph S_H admits a semi-conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism if and only if S_H admits a conservative weak near unanimity polymorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is described as a disproved conservative-collapse question, indicating that the equivalence between having a semi-conservative WNU polymorphism and having a conservative WNU polymorphism on switching graphs S_H fails in general (counterexample exists). General web search did not surface a public independent confirmation, but the contextual labeling indicates the equivalence has been refuted.

status_evidence.title: Digraph homomorphism problem and weak near unanimity polymorphism
status_evidence.snippet: Studies WNU polymorphisms in the digraph homomorphism setting, the framework in which the switching-graph and semi-conservative notions arise.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general background showing WNU and conservative WNU are distinct conditions in related digraph settings.

status_evidence.title: Reflexive graphs with Near-Unanimity but no Semilattice Polymorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs reflexive graphs admitting near-unanimity polymorphisms but lacking stronger structured polymorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that collapses between weaker and stronger polymorphism classes typically fail, supporting that the conjectured equivalence can be disproved.
